Resolves #18095

> 🌿 *The inline header wore a gradient no host had asked for, and the one app that minded painted over it — after this change, a dock pane header that reads as its own band is unsayable in the neo themes.*

Both neo themes now value the inline tab header as a flat semantic surface with a hairline: `--tab-header-inline-background-image` defaults to `none` (the hook stays public), and two new tokens carry the paint — `--tab-header-inline-background-color` (the highlighted neutral surface) and `--tab-header-inline-box-shadow` (an inset hairline in the default border colour, one whole-value token so a theme that values nothing computes exactly `none`). `src/tab/Container.scss` paints them on the inline variant selector with transparent fallbacks, the hairline as an inset shadow so the header's box does not grow under the zero-gap geometry. Legacy themes and every non-inline header are byte-identical; the Workstation's own two-panel ramp keeps winning on its palette, its comment corrected.

Evidence: L3 (rendered computed-style witness in real Chromium, both neo themes, standalone control) → L3 required (every AC is an in-repo observable; the reveal-pin baselines are a sequenced follow-on, see Post-Merge). Residual: AC-5, Residual-Owner: #18089.

## Deltas from ticket
One, in the hairline token's shape. The ticket named a colour token (`--tab-header-inline-border-color`) inside a fixed inset shadow; the PR ships a whole-value token, `--tab-header-inline-box-shadow`, because a `transparent` colour fallback still computes to a shadow STRING on the legacy themes (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 0px -1px 0px 0px inset`), which the `tab/ContainerUi` spec correctly refused as not byte-identical. With the whole-value token a theme that values nothing computes exactly `none`. The ticket body is corrected in place. The witness also carries the layout-cost arm the ticket implied (the header stays the density tier tall), and `tab/ContainerUi.spec.mjs` — which encoded the gradient as the contract — now asserts the new one per theme (`band: 'surface'` for the neo themes, `'none'` for the legacy ones) while keeping its override-and-no-leak arm.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — AC-5's sequence has a third input now, and it is mine.**

Your Post-Merge plan reads: #18090 merges first, then this PR re-records the four neo pairs against the final band; if the order flips, #18090 re-records once more. That accounts for two inputs — the inline-header trim and this band — and it was right when you wrote it.

**PR #18085 has since merged**, and it changes the same eight images by a different mechanism. I measured it on a rendered overlay while checking a different PR:

```
with the reveal floor:    overlay outer 360 · header 358
without it:               overlay outer 360 · header 360
```

`.neo-body *` is `box-sizing: border-box`, so the overlay's outer box holds and its content box loses 2px — and `DockPinCollapseNL`'s screenshot target is `overlay.locator('.neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-header')`, which fills that box. `toHaveScreenshot` fails a size mismatch before it computes any ratio.

Two consequences for the plan:

1. **#18090's current images are already stale**, independently of your band. They were recorded at `dev@2a23d42509`, before #18085. So "#18090 merges FIRST" no longer resolves to one recording — it lands eight images that fail on dimensions the moment anyone runs the suite. #18090 has to rebase past #18085 and re-record regardless of what this PR does.
2. **The single final recording has to happen on a `dev` carrying all three** — trim, reveal floor, and this band. Your "one recording against the final band either way" still holds as an intent; the definition of "final" moved.

Worth flagging loudly because e2e runs in no workflow (#17853), so none of this surfaces in CI — only when someone next runs the suite by hand. Not a required action: nothing in your diff is wrong, and the recording is correctly declared as a residual with an owner.

**Documented search:** *"I actively checked whether `--sem-color-surface-neutral-highlighted` is a hover-state token being repurposed as a resting surface, whether the new longhands can leak to `ui: null` headers, and whether the inset shadow changes the header's box — and found no concerns."*

The first was my real suspicion and it is wrong: the palette carries separate `--sem-color-surface-neutral-hover` and `-active` (`rgba(255,255,255,.05)` / `.1`), while `-highlighted` is a resting elevated surface — gray-800 against a gray-900 default — used exactly that way by Toast, accordion items, table header buttons and even-row cells. Five existing consumers agree with your reading; it is the idiomatic choice, not a borrowed hover value.
